page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, though it lacks any integrated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most standard compute and memory workloads. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 2204.79 and 16997.2 respectively, placing them in the middle 50% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests recorded 1217.74 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 129.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in single-threaded compression and decompression, with gzip compression reaching 35.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.92 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Additionally, the hardware supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contributes to a top-tier text generation speed of 354.35 tokens/sec during small-model LLM inference.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D16ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon processing with fast local NVMe storage. This configuration mitigates the need for external storage attachments for disk-intensive operations, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training. The instance is suited for workloads such as relational databases, web serving, intermediate-scale ETL pipelines, and lightweight LLM inference tasks that benefit from AMX instruction sets without requiring dedicated GPU hardware.
